title: Cómo cobrar a tus pacientes de forma automática y sin conversaciones incómodas
summary: Descubre cómo sacar el cobro del espacio terapéutico con automatización, tarifas diferenciadas y recordatorios que funcionan solos. La guía honesta para profesionales de salud con Encuadrado.
body_text: Hay una conversación que casi ningún profesional de salud quiere tener: la del cobro. Estás en el espacio terapéutico, justo cuando la sesión terminó, cuando el paciente está todavía procesando algo importante, y de repente toca hablar de dinero. O peor: el paciente se olvidó de pagar, y ahora tienes que recordárselo por WhatsApp sin que parezca que solo te importa eso. Es incómodo, y no debería serlo, pero es parte de la vida del profesional independiente. Cobrar bien no contradice ejercer bien tu profesión, al contrario: un encuadre económico claro y un proceso de cobro ordenado es parte de lo que sostiene una consulta clínica sana, para ti y para tus pacientes. ¿Por qué cuesta tanto cobrar? La incomodidad alrededor del cobro en salud tiene raíces muy concretas. Muchos profesionales de salud sienten una tensión genuina entre la naturaleza del vínculo terapéutico y la transacción económica. Hay una voz interna que dice que hablar de dinero con un paciente que está pasando por algo difícil se siente fuera de lugar, casi como una falta de respeto al proceso. A eso se suma que en Chile hay una cultura del cobro que rara vez se enseña en la formación universitaria. Nadie explica cómo establecer tarifas, cómo comunicarlas, cuándo cobrar o cómo manejar la situación cuando alguien no paga. Se aprende solo, sobre la marcha, con todas las incomodidades que eso implica. El resultado es que muchos profesionales terminan cobrando de forma inconsistente, postergando el cobro para no incomodar, haciendo excepciones que se convierten en regla, o simplemente evitando la conversación hasta que la deuda se vuelve difícil de ignorar. Porqué definir una política de cobro es parte de tu consulta clínica En psicología se habla mucho del encuadre: el conjunto de condiciones que sostienen el espacio terapéutico. El horario, la frecuencia, la modalidad, la confidencialidad. El cobro es parte de ese encuadre, aunque no siempre se piense así. Cuando el pago no está claro, cuando las reglas cambian según el humor del día o la historia que traiga el paciente, cuando la conversación de cobro invade el espacio de la sesión, eso tiene efectos en la dinámica terapéutica. La claridad económica, paradójicamente, protege la relación. Y no se trata de ser inflexible o frío, sino de tener reglas claras que sean iguales para todos, comunicadas desde el inicio, sin tener que renegociarlas cada vez. ¿Cómo sacar el cobro del espacio terapéutico? La mejor solución al problema del cobro incómodo no es aprender a hablar de dinero de forma más natural durante la sesión, es sacar esa conversación del espacio terapéutico por completo. Cuando el cobro está automatizado, no hay momento incómodo. No hay que recordarle nada a nadie en persona. No hay WhatsApps tarde en la noche. El proceso ocurre solo, antes o después de la sesión, y tú puedes estar completamente presente en lo que importa: la atención. Así es como funciona en Encuadrado: El paciente paga al momento de agendar: Cuando configuras tu servicio con cobro previo, el paciente paga en el momento que reserva su sesión. Cuando llega a la consulta, el tema económico ya está resuelto. No hay nada que cobrar, no hay nada que recordar. Si no pagó antes, el recordatorio llega automáticamente: Para quienes prefieren cobrar después de la sesión o tienen pacientes con tarifas especiales, Encuadrado envía automáticamente un link de cobro por correo o WhatsApp. El paciente recibe el aviso y paga cuando puede, sin que tú tengas que escribirle ni hacer seguimiento manual. Puedes cobrar diferenciado sin conversaciones incómodas: Si tienes pacientes con tarifas especiales, ya sea porque llevan mucho tiempo contigo, porque están en un momento económico difícil o porque el servicio que les ofreces es distinto, Encuadrado te permite crear servicios ocultos con precios diferenciados o generar cupones de descuento personalizados. El paciente accede a su tarifa sin que sea necesario negociar nada en el momento. Tienes visibilidad de quién debe y quién no: Desde la sección de Finanzas puedes ver en cualquier momento el estado de cobro de todos tus pacientes: quién pagó, quién tiene sesiones pendientes de pago, cuánto se debe en total. Sin revisar mensajes, sin intentar recordar conversaciones pasadas. Las preguntas que nadie se anima a hacer en voz alta ¿Cobro antes o después de la sesión? Ambos modelos funcionan, y depende mucho de tu especialidad y tu estilo de trabajo. El cobro previo tiene la ventaja de eliminar completamente la conversación de dinero en la sesión y reduce las inasistencias, porque el paciente ya tiene algo comprometido. El cobro posterior puede funcionar mejor en contextos donde el vínculo ya está establecido y la confianza es alta. Lo importante es elegir uno y ser consistente. ¿Qué hago cuando un paciente no paga? Lo primero es no dejar que la deuda se acumule. Un recordatorio automático enviado con tiempo es mucho más efectivo que una conversación directa semanas después. Si la deuda persiste, la conversación es necesaria, pero puede ocurrir fuera del espacio terapéutico: por correo, por mensaje, con calma y sin mezclarla con el contenido de las sesiones. ¿Está bien hacer excepciones? Sí, pero con criterio. Una excepción puntual y comunicada de forma clara es muy distinta a una política implícita de cobrar según las circunstancias. Si decides ofrecer una tarifa diferente a alguien, hazlo de forma explícita y con un mecanismo claro, no como algo que simplemente "quedó así". Encuadrado te da las herramientas para hacer eso de forma ordenada sin que implique una conversación incómoda cada vez. ¿Puedo subir mis tarifas sin perder pacientes? Sí. Y comunicarlo bien es parte de hacerlo bien. Un correo masivo enviado con anticipación, a todos tus pacientes activos, explicando el cambio con respeto y claridad, es mucho más efectivo que comunicarlo en el momento de la sesión o dejar que el paciente se entere cuando va a pagar. Encuadrado te permite hacer ese envío directamente desde la plataforma, segmentado a quienes corresponde. Cobro transparente en consulta: cómo impacta en la relación terapéutica Hay una creencia instalada en muchos profesionales de salud de que poner el tema del dinero en primer plano daña la relación con el paciente. La experiencia de quienes llevan años trabajando con un sistema claro dice lo contrario. Cuando las reglas económicas están definidas desde el inicio, cuando el proceso de cobro es transparente y no depende de conversaciones incómodas, la relación terapéutica tiene más espacio para ser lo que debe ser. El paciente sabe qué esperar, tú sabes qué cobrar, y ninguno de los dos tiene que usar energía en eso dentro de la sesión. Cobrar bien no es lo opuesto de atender bien. Es parte de lo mismo. ‍

title: Core Hours Hubs for Singapore Teams
summary: Why core hours matter for Singapore’s hybrid teams In Singapore, the workday can move fast: early client calls with Australia, late check-ins with Europe, lunchtime travel between Raffles Place and Buona Vista, and a steady stream of regional collaboration across Southeast Asia. For professionals, founders, HR leaders, and business travelers, flexibility is no longer a […] The post Core Hours Hubs for Singapore Teams appeared first on Deskimo .
body_text: Why core hours matter for Singapore’s hybrid teams In Singapore, the workday can move fast: early client calls with Australia, late check-ins with Europe, lunchtime travel between Raffles Place and Buona Vista, and a steady stream of regional collaboration across Southeast Asia. For professionals, founders, HR leaders, and business travelers, flexibility is no longer a perk; it is part of how productive teams operate. But flexibility without structure can quickly become calendar chaos. That is where core hours help. Core hours give teams a shared window for meetings, decision-making, and collaboration, while preserving the freedom to work remotely, start earlier, finish later, or use workspaces closer to home. In Singapore’s dense, well-connected business environment, pairing core hours with distributed work hubs can make hybrid work feel coordinated rather than complicated. What core hours look like in a Singapore hybrid work model Core hours are a defined block of time when team members are expected to be reachable and available for synchronous work. Outside that window, employees may have more flexibility to focus, commute off-peak, manage caregiving responsibilities, or work from a location that suits the day’s priorities. For example, a Singapore-based company might set core hours from 10:00am to 3:00pm, Monday to Thursday. During that period, teams schedule key meetings, stakeholder updates, brainstorming sessions, and approvals. Before and after that window, people can handle deep work, admin, regional calls, or personal commitments. Why the model fits Singapore’s work culture Singapore’s workforce is highly connected, digitally enabled, and accustomed to cross-border business. Many teams support clients or colleagues across ASEAN, China, India, Australia, Europe, and the US. A rigid nine-to-six schedule often does not reflect how work actually happens. At the same time, Singapore professionals still value reliability, responsiveness, and clarity. Core hours provide that balance. They give managers confidence that collaboration will happen, while giving employees practical flexibility around commute times, family needs, and focus work. The approach also aligns with Singapore’s broader move toward flexible work arrangements. The Ministry of Manpower provides guidance on flexible work arrangements in Singapore , reflecting how employers are being encouraged to build more adaptable and sustainable workplace practices. Common core hours patterns for local teams There is no single best schedule. The right model depends on industry, customer expectations, time zones, and team workflows. However, several patterns work well for Singapore-based organisations: 10:00am to 3:00pm for office-based and hybrid corporate teams that want to avoid peak-hour commuting while preserving a strong collaboration window. 11:00am to 4:00pm for regional teams that need more overlap with India, Europe, or Australia. 9:30am to 1:30pm for teams with many parents, caregivers, or employees who prefer early deep-work blocks. Tuesday to Thursday core hours for companies that reserve Mondays and Fridays for remote focus work, planning, or client travel. Project-based core hours for product launches, audits, sales campaigns, or quarterly planning periods. The key is consistency. Once a rhythm is set, employees can plan their week more effectively and managers can reduce the friction of constant scheduling negotiation. How workspace hubs make core hours easier to follow A core hours policy is only useful if employees have practical places to work during that shared window. In Singapore, this is especially important because not every home is ideal for professional calls, confidential work, or long focus sessions. Space constraints, household noise, and shared living arrangements can all affect productivity. Workspace hubs solve this problem by giving teams access to professional environments near MRT stations, business districts, residential areas, and client locations. Instead of forcing everyone to commute to one central headquarters, companies can create a network of convenient places where people can work during core hours. From fixed office to distributed access Traditional office planning assumes that productivity happens in one primary location. Hybrid work challenges that assumption. A sales manager may need to work near a client in Orchard. A developer may prefer a quiet workspace near Tampines. A regional director may need a reliable desk between airport transfers and meetings in the CBD. With distributed hubs, employees choose the most practical location for the work they need to do. This makes core hours more realistic because people are not losing excessive time commuting across the island just to join meetings they could attend from a closer professional workspace. Companies exploring this approach can learn from broader hybrid planning strategies, such as using access and usage signals to improve decisions. Deskimo’s guide on badge data for smarter hybrid space planning explains how organisations can move beyond guesswork when designing flexible workplace systems. What employees need from a good hub Not all workspaces are equally suitable for core hours. A convenient location matters, but so do reliability, privacy, and the ability to support different work modes. Singapore professionals often move between video calls, individual work, client meetings, and quick travel between appointments. A good hub should support all of those needs. Reliable Wi-Fi for video meetings, cloud tools, and real-time collaboration. Quiet zones or phone booths for confidential calls and focused work. Meeting rooms for team discussions, onboarding, interviews, and client presentations. Easy transport access near MRT stations, bus routes, or major commercial areas. Flexible booking so employees can reserve space only when they need it. Professional amenities such as power access, ergonomic seating, printing, and refreshments. For business travelers, these features are more than conveniences. They can determine whether a day between meetings is productive or wasted. For local employees, they reduce the stress of choosing between a noisy home environment and a long commute to headquarters. Designing core hours without creating meeting overload One common mistake is treating core hours as a block to fill with meetings. That defeats the purpose. The shared window should improve collaboration, not create back-to-back calls that leave people exhausted and unable to do meaningful work. The best hybrid teams are intentional. They decide which activities require real-time interaction and which can happen asynchronously. This helps protect energy, reduce unnecessary meetings, and make office or hub time more valuable. Decide what belongs inside the shared window Core hours should be reserved for work that benefits from live conversation. In Singapore’s fast-moving business environment, this often includes client decisions, leadership alignment, project handovers, creative problem-solving, and cross-functional issue resolution. Good uses of core hours include: Weekly team stand-ups where blockers are surfaced and priorities are clarified. Project decision meetings that require input from multiple departments. Client calls involving commercial, technical, and account stakeholders. Onboarding sessions for new hires who need context and relationship-building. Workshops, retrospectives, and planning sessions where real-time discussion improves outcomes. Less suitable activities include routine status updates, information sharing, simple approvals, and one-way announcements. These can often be handled through shared documents, project management tools, or recorded updates. Create rules that make flexibility sustainable A strong policy does not need to be complex, but it should remove ambiguity. Employees should know when they are expected to be available, how meetings should be scheduled, and what flexibility exists outside the shared window. Consider setting simple team norms such as: No recurring meetings before 10:00am unless required for regional or client reasons. No meetings during lunch unless agreed in advance. Meeting-free focus blocks outside the shared window. Clear response-time expectations for chat and email. One shared calendar label for core hours meetings. Default documentation for decisions, especially when some team members cannot attend. These norms are particularly useful for regional teams. A Singapore headquarters may coordinate with colleagues in Kuala Lumpur, Hong Kong, Sydney, Manila, Jakarta, and Bengaluru. Without explicit rules, employees can feel pulled across time zones all day. With clear core hours, collaboration becomes more predictable. Regional examples can also help teams think beyond one central office. For instance, the concept of convenient city-based workpoints is explored in Deskimo’s article on mall work hubs for Hong Kong teams , which highlights how everyday commercial locations can become practical support for hybrid work. Planning workspace access around core hours Once a company defines its shared collaboration window, the next step is operational planning. Where should people work from? How often should teams meet in person? What kind of space should the company provide? These questions matter because the wrong setup can turn a good policy into an expensive compromise. Singapore’s commercial real estate costs, compact geography, and excellent transport system create an opportunity to be more precise. Instead of assuming every employee needs a permanent desk, companies can match workspace access to actual patterns of use. Use demand patterns, not assumptions Hybrid work often fails when companies rely on outdated occupancy assumptions. Leaders may lease too much office space because they fear employees will not have enough room. Or they may cut too aggressively, leaving teams without reliable places to meet during peak collaboration days. A smarter approach is to track demand by day, time, team, and location. For example, a company may find that: Most collaboration happens from Tuesday to Thursday. Meeting rooms are more important than permanent desks. Employees prefer hubs near home on Mondays and Fridays. Sales and client-facing teams need workspace near CBD locations. Product and operations teams benefit from occasional full-day workshops. This data allows companies to provide better access without overcommitting to fixed space. It also helps HR and workplace teams justify decisions with evidence rather than personal preference. Cost discipline is a growing priority for hybrid organisations across the region. Deskimo’s analysis of cutting empty desk costs in Australia offers useful lessons for Singapore companies that want to reduce wasted office spend while maintaining employee choice. Match hubs to employee journeys The most effective hub strategy starts with how people actually move through their workweek. In Singapore, commuting patterns differ widely depending on whether someone lives in Jurong, Woodlands, Serangoon, Tampines, or the city fringe. A single headquarters may be convenient for some employees and inefficient for others. When planning hub access, consider these employee journeys: Home-nearby focus days: Employees work from a professional hub close to home to avoid long commutes while maintaining productivity. Client-meeting days: Employees book a workspace near a client office before or after meetings. Team collaboration days: Teams gather in a central location for workshops or planning sessions. Business travel days: Regional visitors use flexible workspaces between hotel check-out, meetings, and flights. Confidential work days: Employees choose a quiet professional setting instead of taking sensitive calls from home or public cafés. This is where workspace flexibility becomes a practical business tool. It supports productivity while respecting the realities of modern working life. Managing people, performance, and trust during core hours A successful core hours system is not only a scheduling decision. It is also a trust decision. Managers need to shift from measuring presence to measuring outcomes. Employees need to communicate clearly and use flexibility responsibly. HR leaders need to design policies that are fair, inclusive, and easy to understand. Singapore’s workforce is diverse, with multinational companies, SMEs, startups, government-linked organisations, and independent professionals all operating in close proximity. A one-size-fits-all policy rarely works. The strongest approach combines clear expectations with room for team-level adaptation. Measure outcomes instead of online presence One risk of hybrid work is digital presenteeism, where employees feel pressure to appear constantly online. This can be just as unhealthy as office presenteeism. Core hours should reduce that pressure by making availability expectations explicit. Managers can support this shift by focusing on: Deliverables completed, not hours visibly online. Quality of collaboration during agreed windows. Customer response standards and service outcomes. Project milestones and team commitments. Employee wellbeing and sustainable workload levels. Singapore’s digital economy and high-connectivity environment make flexible work more feasible, but technology alone is not enough. The Infocomm Media Development Authority’s work on Singapore’s digital economy highlights the importance of digital adoption, yet teams still need human-centred norms to make hybrid work effective. Support fairness across different roles Not every employee has the same flexibility. Some roles require customer coverage, physical presence, secure systems, or specific equipment. A fair policy acknowledges these differences rather than pretending they do not exist. For HR teams, the goal is to create principles that are consistent while allowing operational variation. For example, a finance team may need fixed availability during month-end closing. A customer support team may need staggered shifts. A product team may prefer fewer meetings and longer focus blocks. To keep the system fair, document the reasons for different arrangements and review them regularly. Employees are more likely to accept variation when the logic is transparent. Companies with cross-border teams can also learn from neighbouring markets. Deskimo’s article on claim-ready work hubs for Malaysia teams is a useful reference for organisations thinking about how flexible workspace access can support employee mobility and reimbursement processes. Practical steps to launch a core hours hub strategy Launching a core hours model does not require a major transformation programme. It works best as a structured pilot: start small, test assumptions, gather feedback, and refine the policy before scaling. For Singapore teams, a pilot can often be run within one department, project group, or regional function. The goal is to learn what improves productivity and what creates friction. A good pilot should answer practical questions about timing, workspace demand, meeting quality, employee satisfaction, and manager confidence. Step one: define the collaboration window Start by choosing a simple schedule. Avoid creating too many exceptions at the beginning. A clear window such as 10:00am to 3:00pm, Tuesday to Thursday, is easier to test than a complicated rotating schedule. Before finalising the window, review: Customer and client availability. Regional time-zone overlap. School drop-off and caregiving patterns. Peak commute times. Existing meeting volume. Team preferences and operational constraints. It is also worth considering wider labour and workforce trends. The Department of Statistics Singapore publishes labour and population data through SingStat , which can help leaders understand the broader context of workforce participation, demographics, and employment patterns. Step two: map workspace needs Once the time window is clear, identify where people need to work. This is where many companies discover that flexibility is not only about remote work. It is about giving employees access to the right environment for the task. Ask employees which locations would help them use core hours most effectively. Options may include central business districts, residential hubs, city-fringe areas, or locations near major transport nodes. For business travelers, include airport access, hotel districts, and meeting-heavy commercial zones. Then group workspace needs into categories: Individual desks for focused work. Small rooms for video calls and confidential conversations. Meeting rooms for team collaboration. Event or workshop spaces for larger gatherings. On-demand access for employees who travel across the city. Step three: set communication rules A hub strategy will not work if communication expectations remain unclear. Employees should know when they need to be reachable, when they can focus, and how urgent matters should be escalated. Useful rules include: Schedule important meetings during the shared window by default. Record or document decisions for anyone who cannot attend. Use asynchronous updates for routine information sharing. Respect focus time outside core hours unless there is a genuine urgency. Encourage teams to state whether a message requires immediate action or can wait. These simple habits reduce stress and make flexibility more inclusive. They also help managers avoid accidentally recreating a full-day meeting culture in a remote setting. Step four: measure and refine After four to eight weeks, review the pilot. Look at both quantitative and qualitative signals. Attendance data and workspace usage matter, but so do employee comments, manager observations, and client outcomes. Useful questions include: Did core hours make meetings easier to schedule? Did employees feel more productive outside the shared window? Were workspace hubs available in the right locations? Did teams reduce unnecessary meetings? Were clients or stakeholders better served? Did managers feel they had enough visibility without micromanaging? Use the answers to adjust the schedule, improve hub coverage, or clarify policy language. The best systems evolve with the business. Building a better hybrid rhythm in Singapore Core hours give Singapore teams a practical way to combine flexibility with accountability. They create a shared rhythm for collaboration while leaving room for deep work, regional coordination, caregiving, travel, and personal productivity. When supported by convenient workspace hubs, the model becomes even stronger because employees can choose professional environments that fit their day. For HR leaders, this means better policy design. For managers, it means clearer expectations and fewer scheduling battles. For freelancers, entrepreneurs, and business travelers, it means access to structure without sacrificing mobility. In a compact, globally connected market like Singapore, that balance can be a real competitive advantage. The most effective approach is simple: define the shared window, protect it from meeting overload, provide flexible workspace access, measure real usage, and refine the model over time. Teams that do this well can reduce wasted office space, improve employee experience, and make hybrid work feel deliberate rather than improvised. title: Why Closed Source Integration Platforms Are an AI Agent Security Risk
summary: Why closed source integration platforms are a security risk for AI agents — and how open source TypeScript frameworks with self-hosted options give you the auditability multi-tenant AI products need.
body_text: When an AI agent connects to Gmail, Slack, Stripe, or a CRM on behalf of your users, something has to manage the tokens, the permissions, and the actual API calls underneath. Many teams reach for a closed source integration platform to handle this because it looks like the fastest path to shipping. The problem shows up later, once real customers and real credentials are flowing through infrastructure you cannot see inside of. A closed platform asks you to trust a black box with your users' Gmail tokens, their Stripe access, and every action your agent takes on their behalf, with no way to verify how that trust is actually being handled. This post looks at why that tradeoff is riskier than it first appears, how closed and open integration layers differ in practice, and what it actually takes to handle authentication safely when you are building a multi-tenant AI agent platform. Understanding Closed Integration Layers vs Open Source TypeScript Frameworks A closed integration platform sells you convenience. You get an API, some documentation, and a promise that token refresh, webhook handling, and provider quirks are all taken care of. What you do not get is the ability to see how any of it actually works. This matters more for AI agents than it did for typical SaaS integrations, for a few reasons: You cannot audit what you cannot see. If a closed platform has a vulnerability in how it isolates tenants, encrypts credentials, or validates webhook signatures, you will not know until something breaks. With an open source TypeScript framework, the code is right there. Your security team, or anyone else's, can read exactly how tokens are stored and resolved. Roadmap dependency becomes a business risk. If a closed platform does not support an integration your product needs, you wait. You file a request and hope it gets prioritized. An open project lets you open a pull request or fork the repository and add exactly what you need, on your own timeline. Vendor lock in compounds over time. The longer your agent's integration logic lives inside a closed platform's proprietary format, the harder it becomes to migrate away if pricing changes, support quality drops, or the vendor shuts down. Open source projects built on standard TypeScript keep your integration code portable. Security through obscurity is not security. Closed platforms sometimes lean on the idea that hidden code is safer because attackers cannot study it. In practice, this just means fewer eyes are checking for problems before they get exploited, not that the problems do not exist. Self Hosted vs Managed Integration Layers for Multi Tenant AI Products: Key Differences Once you are convinced open source matters, the next decision is whether to self host your integration layer or use a managed version of it. Both are valid, and the right choice depends on your team's constraints, not a blanket rule. Self hosted gives you full control over data residency. Every token, every cached record, and every API call stays inside the infrastructure you already operate. For products handling sensitive data, or teams under strict compliance requirements, this is often the deciding factor. Corsair, for example, lets teams run the full SDK on their own infrastructure at no cost, with no data leaving their stack. Managed removes operational overhead. Running token refresh jobs, webhook listeners, and encrypted storage reliably at scale takes real engineering time. A managed version of an open source integration layer gives you that infrastructure without asking your team to own it, while still leaving you the option to move to self hosting later since the code underneath is the same. Both should use the same open source core. The real advantage of choosing an open source integration layer is that self hosted and managed are not two different products with two different security models. They are the same codebase, so you can start managing to move fast, then migrate to self hosted later without rewriting your integration logic. Cost structure differs meaningfully at scale. Closed managed platforms often charge per seat or per connection in ways that scale unpredictably. Open source options with a self hosted path let you avoid vendor markup on API calls you are already paying for once your usage passes a certain point. Support model changes what you are actually buying. A closed platform sells you a black box with a support ticket queue behind it. An open source project gives you the code plus a community, so even without a support contract, you are not fully dependent on one vendor's response time. Building a B2B AI Agent Platform, How Do You Handle User Authentication Safely? If you are building a B2B AI agent platform, authentication is not a single problem. It is at least three problems stacked on top of each other: authenticating your own users into your product, authenticating your agent to act on behalf of a specific tenant, and authenticating that tenant's connected third party accounts like Gmail or Salesforce. A few practices consistently separate safe implementations from risky ones: Isolate credentials per tenant, not per app. Every connected account needs a clear tenant boundary. A shared credential pool, even an accidental one caused by a caching bug, is one of the fastest ways to leak one customer's data into another customer's agent session. Never let the model see raw tokens. Your agent should call tools by name and receive results. The actual API key or OAuth token should be resolved behind the scenes, never placed in the context window where a prompt injection attack could expose it. Require approval for sensitive or destructive actions. Reading a calendar is low risk. Sending an email or issuing a refund is not. Route the second category through a review step so a human confirms the action before it executes. Use envelope encryption for stored credentials. A key you control should wrap a per tenant encryption key, which wraps the actual secret. This way, no single leaked key exposes every customer's credentials at once, which is exactly the model Corsair uses for its hosted credential storage. Verify every webhook signature. Third party providers push data to you constantly. If you are not verifying that a webhook actually came from the provider it claims to be from, you are trusting an unauthenticated input path directly into your system. Treat authentication as infrastructure, not a feature. Teams that bolt authentication onto an existing agent as an afterthought tend to end up with inconsistent handling across integrations. Building it as a shared layer from the start keeps every tool call held to the same standard. Why Choose an Open Source TypeScript Framework for Your Application? TypeScript has become the default language for a huge share of application backends, which makes an open source TypeScript integration framework a natural fit for teams already working in that ecosystem. A few concrete reasons this choice pays off: Type safety catches integration bugs before production. When your integration layer is written in TypeScript with proper types for each provider's API, a huge class of bugs, mismatched fields, wrong parameter types, missing required scopes, gets caught at compile time instead of at runtime in front of a customer. You can read the exact code handling your users' data. There is no ambiguity about what happens when your agent calls a tool. You can trace the request from your application code through the integration layer to the third party API and back. Extending it does not require waiting on anyone. Need a plugin for an integration that does not exist yet? With an open project like Corsair, you can scaffold a new plugin with one command and build it yourself, or open a pull request so the maintainers merge it for everyone. It fits naturally into existing developer workflows. Your team already reviews TypeScript code, already tests TypeScript code, and already deploys TypeScript code. An integration framework in the same language slots into that workflow instead of asking you to learn a new proprietary configuration system. Community scrutiny improves security over time. Thousands of developers reading and contributing to the same codebase tend to catch problems faster than a small closed team working alone, simply because more people are looking at the same code from more angles. Closed source integration platforms ask you to hand over trust you cannot verify, and for an AI agent acting on real customer accounts, that is a trust you cannot afford to give blindly. The safer path is an open source integration layer where the authentication, permissions, and credential storage are all code you or your security team can actually read. Corsair was built around exactly this idea, an open source TypeScript framework for multi-tenant integrations that you can self host for free or run managed, with the same auditable code either way. Whichever path fits your team, choosing openness over a black box is what lets you scale an AI agent platform without scaling your exposure to risk right alongside it. Corsair.dev Read the docs →

title: Nail Gun Safety Tips for Siding Projects
summary: Learn essential nail gun safety tips for siding projects, including proper setup, protective gear, common mistakes to avoid, and best practices for creating a safer jobsite.
body_text: For many siding projects, a nail gun is one of the most essential and frequently used tools on the job site. They help speed up projects, improve efficiency, and reduce the physical strain of driving nails by hand. Whether you're installing siding on a new build, remodeling an exterior, or tackling a backyard structure, a nail gun can help you get the job done faster. While nail guns can help improve efficiency and speed up siding installation, they also present safety risks if not used properly. At LP, safety is one of our core values, which is why understanding proper nail gun handling, setup, and jobsite safety practices is essential for helping prevent accidents, reduce risk, and keep projects running smoothly. Why Nail Guns Are Popular for Siding Installation Nail guns are widely used for siding projects because they can significantly reduce installation time compared to hand nailing. They help create consistent fastening, improve productivity, and make it easier to complete larger projects efficiently. When paired with proper installation techniques and manufacturer recommendations, a nail gun can be a valuable tool for both professionals and first-time users. Understand Common Nail Gun Hazards Before starting a siding project, it's important to understand the most common risks associated with nail gun use. Potential hazards include: Accidental discharge Nail ricochets from hard surfaces or knots in wood Missed fasteners that exit through the back of the material Injuries caused by improper handling or carrying Tripping hazards from hoses, cords, or jobsite clutter Many nail gun injuries occur during routine tasks, making proper training and awareness critical even for experienced users. Wear the Proper Safety Gear Personal protective equipment should always be worn when operating a nail gun. Recommended safety gear includes: Safety glasses with side protection Hearing protection Work gloves Long pants and durable footwear A hard hat when required on active jobsites Eye protection is particularly important because nails, wood chips, and debris can become airborne during installation. Set Up Your Nail Gun Correctly Before beginning work, inspect your equipment and verify that the tool is operating properly. Best practices include: Read and follow the manufacturer's instructions Check hoses, fittings, and connections for damage Ensure the correct nail type and nail length are being used Adjust air pressure according to tool recommendations Test the nail gun on scrap material before installation Taking a few minutes to inspect equipment can help prevent misfires and installation issues later in the project. Create a Safe Work Area A safe workspace is just as important as a safe tool operation. To improve jobsite safety: Keep hoses and extension cords organized Remove unnecessary debris and obstacles Ensure adequate lighting Maintain stable footing when working on ladders or scaffolding Keep bystanders away from active work areas For siding projects that require ladder work, always maintain three points of contact when climbing and avoid overreaching while fastening materials. Best Practices for Safe Nail Gun Use When using a nail gun, focus on controlled and deliberate operation. Follow these guidelines: Keep your finger off the trigger until ready to fire Never point the tool at yourself or others Hold materials securely before fastening Position your free hand away from the nailing path Disconnect the air supply before clearing jams or making adjustments Taking a slower, controlled approach can help prevent many common nail gun accidents. Common Mistakes to Avoid Even experienced users can develop habits that increase safety risks. Avoid: Using a damaged or poorly maintained tool Operating a nail gun without eye and hearing protection Carrying the tool with your finger on the trigger Firing nails too close to material edges Skipping equipment inspections before use Working in cluttered or unstable areas Small mistakes can quickly lead to injuries or installation problems, making attention to detail essential throughout the project. Build Safety Into Every Siding Project Nail guns can make siding installation faster and more efficient, but safe operation should always come first. By wearing the proper protective equipment, maintaining your tools, setting up a safe workspace, and following best practices, you can reduce risk while improving project outcomes. Whether you're installing siding on a home, shed, garage, or outdoor structure, taking time to prioritize safety can help ensure your project is completed successfully and confidently. body_text: Most women look forward to taking off their bra after a long day. While this feeling is common, constant discomfort should never be considered normal. A bra that digs into your shoulders, leaves painful marks, or causes back pain may be more than just an inconvenience. It could be a sign that you are wearing the wrong size. According to experts featured in the source article, a large percentage of women wear bras that do not fit correctly. Poorly fitted bras can contribute to neck pain, shoulder discomfort, poor posture, skin irritation, and unnecessary strain on the body. Despite these issues, bra fitting often receives far less attention than other aspects of personal health. This guide explores why proper bra fitting matters, the health concerns linked to an incorrect fit, and practical ways to choose a bra that supports both comfort and well-being. Why Bra Fit Matters A bra is designed to support breast tissue and distribute weight evenly across the chest and back. When it fits correctly, it helps reduce pressure on the shoulders, improves posture, and provides comfort throughout the day. However, many women continue wearing the same bra size for years without considering that their bodies naturally change over time. Weight fluctuations, pregnancy, breastfeeding, hormonal changes, and aging can all affect breast shape and size. As a result, a bra that once fit perfectly may eventually become uncomfortable and less supportive. Common Health Problems Caused by Poorly Fitted Bras Wearing an incorrect bra size may lead to several physical issues. Neck and Shoulder Pain One of the most common complaints is pain in the neck and shoulders. Many people assume tight shoulder straps are responsible, but experts explain that most support should come from the band around the rib cage rather than the straps. When the band is too loose, the straps carry excessive weight, leading to pressure and soreness. Back Pain Poor support can place extra stress on the muscles of the upper and lower back. Over time, this may contribute to chronic discomfort, particularly for women with larger bust sizes. A properly fitted bra distributes weight more evenly, reducing unnecessary strain on the spine and surrounding muscles. Poor Posture An ill-fitting bra may encourage rounded shoulders and poor posture. Constant discomfort often causes women to adjust their body position throughout the day, which can affect spinal alignment over time. Better support can help maintain a more natural posture during everyday activities. Skin Irritation and Chafing Tight bands, underwires, and rough fabrics can rub against the skin, causing redness, irritation, and painful chafing. Heat and perspiration may make these issues worse, especially during warmer months or after exercise. Pressure Marks Temporary marks from clothing are common, but deep grooves or painful indentations are usually signs that a bra is either too tight or does not fit properly. Persistent pressure may reduce overall comfort and make daily activities unpleasant. Signs Your Bra Does Not Fit Properly Many women accept discomfort because they assume bras are supposed to feel restrictive. In reality, several warning signs suggest it may be time for a professional fitting. These include: Shoulder straps digging into the skin Bands riding up the back Cups that overflow or leave gaps Constant adjustments throughout the day Underwires pressing into breast tissue Pain after only a few hours of wear Red marks that remain for an extended period If you experience one or more of these issues regularly, your current bra size may no longer be suitable. Why So Many Women Wear the Wrong Size Several factors contribute to widespread sizing problems. Many women are measured only once during their teenage years and never again. Unlike eye tests or shoe fittings, bra fittings are rarely treated as part of routine personal care. Sizing also varies between manufacturers. A size that fits well in one brand may feel completely different in another. Body changes over time further complicate the issue. Weight gain, weight loss, pregnancy, menopause, and hormonal cycles can all alter breast shape. How to Check Your Bra Fit Experts recommend paying attention to several key areas. The Band The band should provide most of the support. It should fit snugly around the rib cage without causing discomfort. You should be able to fit two fingers comfortably underneath the band. The Cups Breast tissue should fit completely inside each cup without spilling over the edges or leaving empty spaces. The Underwire If your bra includes an underwire, it should surround the breast rather than pressing into breast tissue. The Straps Straps should stay in place without digging into your shoulders. Their purpose is to stabilize the bra, not carry the majority of breast weight. Fabric Choice Is Also Important Fit is only one part of bra comfort. The material also plays a significant role. Breathable fabrics help reduce moisture buildup, keeping skin cooler and drier throughout the day. Soft materials may also reduce friction, lowering the risk of irritation and chafing. Some brands are developing bras using natural or plant-based fibers that focus on softness and moisture management while providing everyday comfort. Choosing quality materials may improve the wearing experience, particularly for women with sensitive skin. Should You Get Professionally Fitted? Professional bra fittings can help identify sizing issues that are difficult to notice on your own. A trained fitter evaluates band size, cup size, strap adjustment, and overall support. Since body shape changes over time, regular fittings may help ensure continued comfort. Even if you prefer shopping online, getting professionally measured occasionally provides a useful sizing reference. Everyday Tips for Better Bra Comfort Simple habits can improve comfort throughout the day. Replace worn-out bras regularly. Rotate between several bras instead of wearing the same one daily. Wash bras according to care instructions to preserve elasticity. Change out of sweaty sports bras promptly after exercise. Reassess your size after significant weight or hormonal changes. Prioritize comfort over appearance whenever possible. These small adjustments may help reduce discomfort while extending the lifespan of your bras. The Future of Women's Underwear Many industry professionals believe bras should be viewed as an important part of women's health rather than simply a fashion item. Greater awareness, improved sizing standards, better materials, and easier access to professional fittings could help reduce unnecessary pain experienced by millions of women. As conversations around women's health continue to grow, comfortable and supportive underwear is becoming an increasingly important part of overall well-being. Final Thoughts A bra should provide support without causing pain. If you frequently experience neck aches, shoulder discomfort, back pain, skin irritation, or constant adjustments throughout the day, your bra may no longer fit correctly. Taking time to check your size, choose breathable materials, and seek professional fitting when needed can make a noticeable difference in your daily comfort. Small changes today may help prevent unnecessary discomfort in the future while improving both posture and confidence. Source The Independent (July 24, 2026). Disclaimer This article is intended for informational and educational purposes only. It should not be considered medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. If you experience persistent pain, skin irritation, breast changes, or other health concerns, consult a qualified healthcare professional or a certified bra-fitting specialist for personalized guidance.

title: FanDuel and CME Group launch FanDuel Predicts to give customers the power to trade on tomorrow's headlines
body_text: New prediction markets platform launches in five states with a phased expansion to other states through early 2026 NEW YORK AND CHICAGO , December 22, 2025 – Today, FanDuel, the premier online gaming company in North America and part of Flutter Entertainment (NYSE: FLUT, LSE: FLTR), and CME Group (NASDAQ: CME), the world's leading derivatives marketplace, launched FanDuel Predicts in Alabama, Alaska, South Carolina, North Dakota and South Dakota, beginning a phased national rollout over the coming weeks. FanDuel Predicts will expand access to financial and sports markets for millions of U.S. customers over the coming months. FanDuel Predicts will provide customers with a platform to express their views on the day’s biggest stories across financial indicators, cultural moments and sports. This new mobile application will be available in the Apple App Store and Google Play and will integrate FanDuel’s “Know Your Customer” sign-up process, requiring customers to submit their birth date, Social Security number, home address, banking information and a government-issued ID. Once the Predicts account is created, customers can buy or sell event contracts ranging in price from as little as $0.01 to $0.99 by choosing "Yes" if they think an event will happen or "No" if they don't. The platform will offer event contracts in all 50 states on benchmarks such as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, prices of oil and gas, gold, cryptocurrencies, and key economic indicators such as GDP and CPI. In addition to financial markets, sports contracts will be available across baseball, basketball, football, and hockey in states where online sports betting is not yet legal, except on tribal lands. As new states legalize online sports betting, FanDuel Predicts will cease offering sports event contracts in those states. " We're giving our customers a new platform to engage with the world around them - whether that's the next Fed rate decision or a sports event ,” said James Cooper, Senior Vice President, Flywheel and New Ventures at FanDuel . “ This launch in five states will provide valuable insights into customer engagement with this new platform, enabling us to refine our approach as we expand to additional states in 2026 ." “ CME Group prediction markets will enable a new generation of users to express their views on global benchmarks, economic indicators, sports and more ,” said Lynne Fitzpatrick, President and Chief Financial Officer, CME Group . “ This launch is a pivotal step for expanding the reach of our products to FanDuel’s millions of registered users across the U.S .” The rollout of FanDuel Predicts will continue to other states through early 2026. FanDuel will extend its commitment to consumer protection to the FanDuel Predicts app. At launch, customers will be able to set deposit limits, deposit alerts or self-exclude if needed with mental health services provided by Kindbridge Behavior Health. Media Contacts: Alex Pitocchelli, FanDuel: press@fanduel.com

title: Sanctuary Galápagos Penguin: An Aquatic Perfume Inspired by Nature
summary: Discover Sanctuary Galápagos Penguin, an aquatic perfume inspired by the Galápagos Islands with ocean mist, coastal sage, juniper, driftwood, and volcanic amber.
body_text: If you’ve ever wanted a fragrance that smells like the ocean without leaning overly salty, SANCTUARY Galápagos Penguin deserves a spot on your radar. Inspired by one of the world’s most extraordinary ecosystems, this aquatic perfume captures the contrast between cool sea air and volcanic rock to capture the daily life of the creature that moves between sea and stone. What Does SANCTUARY Galápagos Penguin Smell Like? Galápagos Penguin opens with the crisp freshness of ocean mist , immediately bringing to mind cool coastal air. Coastal sage and aromatic juniper jump in, adding an invigorating freshness. As the fragrance settles, driftwood creates an earthy foundation while volcanic amber lends a soft warmth, balancing the airy opening with a smooth, long-lasting finish. The result is an aquatic fragrance that’s both refreshing and sophisticated, ideal for anyone who enjoys both clean scents and those inspired by the outdoors. The Story Behind the Fragrance Like the Galápagos penguin itself, this fragrance celebrates resilience and adaptation. The Galápagos penguin is the only penguin species found in the Northern Hemisphere, surviving in a cold environment and chilly seas. Today, however, warming seas, stronger El Niño episodes, pollution, and habitat disruption threaten these remarkable penguins, making conservation efforts more important than ever. Sanctuary ‘s Galápagos Penguin serves as both a beautiful fragrance and a reminder of the delicate ecosystems that continue to inspire. Discover Sanctuary on Scentbird With Scentbird , you can experience Sanctuary Galápagos Penguin before committing to a full-size bottle. If you’re looking for a fresh aquatic perfume that combines ocean air, aromatic greens, and warm woods in a unique composition, this is one you’ll want to add to your queue.

body_text: RICHMOND, Va., July 9, 2026 – Markel has been awarded on TIME’s list of America’s Best Companies 2026. This prestigious award is presented in collaboration with Statista, the world-leading statistics portal and industry ranking provider. The award list was announced on July 9, 2026, and can be viewed on TIME.com . TIME and Statista identified America’s Best Companies 2026 based on three primary dimensions: Employee Satisfaction – Based on survey data from approximately 217,000 verified employees at U.S. companies over the past three years, covering company recommendations and employer ratings across image, atmosphere, working conditions, salary, workplace, and equality. Financial Performance – Drawn from Statista's revenue database (last five years). Companies needed at least US $100 million in revenue in 2025. Performance was assessed on multiple metrics: short-term (2023–2025) and long-term (2021–2025) revenue growth (relative and absolute), changes in net income, asset growth, and the evolution of return on assets (ROA), all for 2023–2025. Sustainability Transparency – Based on an ESG index from Statista's ESG Database and additional research, covering: Environmental : 2024 carbon emissions intensity, reduction rate versus 2022, and CDP score Social : Share of women on the board and existence of a human rights policy Governance : Presence of a GRI-aligned CSR report and a compliance/anti-corruption policy The 1,000 highest-scoring companies were recognized as America’s Best Companies 2026. Based on the results of the study, Markel is honored to be recognized on TIME’s list of America’s Best Companies 2026. Statista publishes hundreds of worldwide industry rankings and company listings with high-profile media partners. This research and analysis service is based on the success of Statista.com , the leading data and business intelligence portal that provides statistics, relevant business data, and various market and consumer studies and surveys. title: US Army Awards L3Harris NGC2 Manpack Radio Delivery Orders
summary: L3Harris Technologies has received orders totaling $84 million in support of the U.S. Army for Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) manpack Falcon® systems.
body_text: ROCHESTER, N.Y., June 9, 2026 — L3Harris Technologies (NYSE: LHX) has received orders totaling $84 million in support of the U.S. Army for Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) manpack Falcon® systems. The AN/PRC-158C systems include high-throughput Mobile Ad hoc NETworks (MANET) and highly resilient waveforms for assured communications in all conditions. This is L3Harris’ second award in support of NGC2, following an initial $24 million order in October. The manpack systems will serve as part of the program’s transport layer, which is a collection of networks, communication pathways and data-delivery technologies that move information across sensors, shooters and command-and-control systems. “Our Falcon Advanced Data Node gateways are battle-tested, fielded around the world and, with their software-defined architectures, ready for the constantly evolving challenges and threats facing soldiers,” said Chris Aebli, President, Mission Critical Communications, Communications & Spectrum Dominance, L3Harris. “We continue to invest and innovate both our system capabilities and production capacities to meet our global customers’ needs with a commercial business model that perfectly aligns with the U.S. Department of War’s commercial-first acquisition approach.” The communication systems support the requirements of multi-transport gateways necessary to enable NGC2 with features including air-to-ground networking, routing, MANETs, In Line Encryption and Sensitive But Unclassified – Encrypted waveforms. title: How I Use Cocreate on Set
summary: Synced dailies in minutes, notes right away, and no sorting delay before the edit.
body_text: ← All writing On Set · JUL 1 2026 How I Use Cocreate on Set My on-set workflow usually involves a lot of looking back at what we’ve already shot. Especially in the commercial world, we’re often picking up pieces of scenes across different days, sometimes even splitting actors’ coverage over time. I’m constantly referencing previous setups just to make sure everything stays consistent. On bigger projects I’ll have a team helping manage that, but on smaller shoots it’s pretty scrappy: I end up digging through drives, opening a bunch of files until I find the right setup, and grabbing screenshots to use as reference. Reviewing footage has always been the toughest part for me. DITs don’t always have time to turn around synced dailies, so when we’re moving fast I’m stuck watching muted clips straight off a drive and jotting notes in my phone to keep track of things for later. What’s been helpful lately is using Cocreate to process footage while we’re still on set. Once media is backed up, I can run it through and, within a few minutes, have synced dailies ready to watch and start leaving notes on right away. It makes a big difference just being able to review clips properly, with sound, and keep everything organized in one place. Labeling footage is also a lot faster now. Instead of doing it all manually, I can pull from transcripts and slates, then just fix anything that didn’t come through correctly. Being able to search shots by name and have things organized by scene, with notes attached directly to them makes on-set review way more straightforward. By the time the shoot wraps, everything’s already organized enough that I can jump into the edit without that usual delay of sorting and labeling. More than anything, it’s made the whole process feel less chaotic. I have a clearer sense of what I’ve got, and I can get into the edit quicker without second-guessing. Written by Matan Hamam Start Loading Cocreate reads slates, syncs audio by timecode and waveform, detects and groups multicams, builds stringouts, and outputs a Premiere or Avid project to your exact preferences. title: Don't bother parsing: Just use images for RAG
summary: If search is the game, looks matter
body_text: At Morphik, we build RAG tools to provide developers accurate search over complex documents. In this article, we explain why we operate over "images" of pages instead of doing OCR/ parsing. If you’ve ever tried to extract information from a complex PDF: one with charts, diagrams, and tables mixed with text, you know the pain. That invoice with a nested table showing quarterly breakdowns? The research paper whose intricate figures actually contain the key findings? The technical manual where the annotated diagrams explain more than the text ever could? Or maybe the IKEA manual with no text at all. We’ve all been there, watching our carefully crafted parsing pipeline mangle yet another document. The industry’s dirty secret is that we’re spending enormous effort (and money) on OCR, layout detection, and parsing pipelines that still lose the information that matters most. It’s like trying to “watch” a movie by reading its script: you miss all the visual storytelling that makes it meaningful. For example, let’s take a very simple all text page (not scanned, no diagrams, etc.) like the one below: Fig 1: Simple page showing Palantir financials If I try to parse it with common OCR tools (the values might come out correct, but the headings and values all get jumbled up, add on standard chunking, we might not send correct information when retrieving) Q1 Financials US commercial continues to accelerate in Q1 2025 alongside AIP revolution +71% Y/Y +65% Y/Y US Commercial Revenue US Commercial Customer Count +19% Q/Q +13% Q/Q US Commercial Revenue US Commercial Customer Count +127% Y/Y $810M US Commercial Remaining Deal Value 2x Y/Y US Commercial Total Contract Value +30% Q/Q US Commercial Deals Closed of $1M or Greater +183% Y/Y US Commercial Remaining Deal Value US Commercial Total Contract Value 2025 Palantir Technologies Inc. We dene a customer as an organization from which we have recognized revenue during the trailing twelve months period. This is possibly one of the simplest documents, we haven’t even come to complex or technical documents. Note/ Aside: You might still need to convert a document to text or a structured format, that’s essential for syncing information into structured databases or data lakes. In those cases, OCR works (with its quirks), but in my experience passing the original document to an LLM is better (we do this with Morphik workflows, learn more here ). The Traditional Approach: A House of Cards When we started building RAG at Morphik, we did what everyone does: assembled the standard document processing pipeline. You know the one, it starts with OCR and ends with tears. Here's what that "state-of-the-art" pipeline actually looks like: Run OCR on your PDFs (hope it reads the numbers correctly) Deploy layout detection models (hope they identify table boundaries) Reconstruct reading order (hope it follows the visual flow) Caption figures with specialized models (hope they capture the nuance) Chunk text "intelligently" (hope you don't split related info) Generate embeddings with BGE-M3 or similar (hope meaning survives) Store in your vector database (hope you can find it later) Take a simple invoice with a table showing itemized costs. First, your OCR might read "1,000" as "l,0O0" (those are letters, not numbers). Then your layout detector might miss that the subtotal row is actually part of the table. Your chunking strategy splits the table from its header. By the time you're searching for "total costs for Q3," you're searching through mangled text that bears little resemblance to the original document. We once spent six hours debugging why our system couldn't find information that was clearly visible in a financial report. Turns out, the parsing pipeline had interpreted a pie chart's legend as body text, scattering percentages throughout unrelated paragraphs. Even if OCR captured every character flawlessly, the meaning locked inside images, figures, and tables would still vanish. Suppose layout detection nailed every bounding box; you would still rely on figure captioning, and captions inevitably miss critical context. A hybrid approach-feeding text to a text-embedding model and images to an image-embedding model-sounds appealing, yet it shatters the document’s positional context. Queries that depend on spatial relationships (“which part of the diagram labels Q3 total?”) become impossible, embeddings for text and images live in separate spaces, and retrieval pipelines struggle to reconcile them. Positional loss, modality gaps, and fractured semantics compound into answers that feel random. In practice, you still cannot trust the pipeline. The Lightbulb Moment: What If We Just... Looked at the Page? The revelation came during yet another debugging session. Arnav, my co-founder (and brother 🙂) asked the question that changed everything: "Why are we deconstructing these documents just to reconstruct meaning? What if we treated them the way humans do: as visual objects?" It sounds almost too simple. But that's exactly what the recent ColPali research proved possible. Vision Language Models have quietly gotten good enough to understand documents directly . No parsing. No OCR. No reconstruction. Just: Document → Image → Understanding. The elegance is stunning. Instead of seven fragile steps, you have one robust operation. Instead of losing information at every stage, you preserve everything: every chart, every table relationship, every visual cue that makes documents understandable to humans. In Fig 1., what the LLM would “see” in this case is direct page itself, maintaining all positional information! Under the Hood: How Visual Document Retrieval Actually Works Here's where it gets technically interesting. The ColPali model doesn't just "look" at documents. It understands them in a fundamentally different way than traditional approaches. The process is beautifully straightforward: First, we treat each document page as an image, essentially taking a high-resolution screenshot. This image gets divided into patches, like laying a grid over the page. Each patch might contain a few words, part of a chart, or a table cell. A Vision Transformer (specifically SigLIP-So400m) processes these patches, but here's the clever part: instead of trying to extract text, it creates rich embeddings that understand both textual and visual elements in context. These embeddings are then refined by a language model (PaliGemma-3B) that's been trained to understand document structure. When you search for "Q3 revenue trends," the magic happens through what's called "late interaction." The model doesn't just look for those exact words, it finds patches containing the text "Q3," the word "revenue," but also the relevant parts of charts showing upward trends, table cells with quarterly figures, and even color-coded elements that indicate performance. It's like having a human expert who can instantly scan every page and understand not just what's written, but what's shown . An interesting overview of ColPali by Arnav here. (more to scratch the technical itch) Fig 3: Comparison of traditional pipelines vs ColPali Real-World Showdown: Morphik vs. The Alternatives When we built Morphik, we implemented ColPali and quickly discovered that productizing it was far more complex than the research suggested. No vector database directly supported our desired similarity function at that time, and every provider offered optimizations for single vectors instead of multi-vectors, which was painfully slow. We added optimizations like binary quantization and then using Hamming distance for calculation instead of dot product, among other performance improvements... each piece had hidden complexity. But the real test came when we compared our approach to existing solutions. Systematic Evaluation: The Numbers Don't Lie To validate these observations beyond anecdotal evidence, we worked with TLDC (The LLM Data Company) to build an open-source financial document benchmark with 45 challenging questions across NVIDIA 10-Qs, Palantir investor presentations, and JPMorgan reports. TLDC has a complex multistep process for generating these evaluations, and their objective was frankly to humiliate us. They wanted questions that would expose the limitations of any document retrieval system. The evaluation harness is designed to be easy to use, and anyone can test their RAG system against these same questions and see how they stack up. The results were striking: while other end-to-end providers peaked at around 67% accuracy, and even a carefully optimized custom LangChain pipeline with semantic chunking and OpenAI's text-embedding-large model achieved 72%, Morphik delivered 95.56% accuracy on the same evaluation set. For comparison, OpenAI's file search tools, which represents a solid baseline, managed only 13.33% accuracy on these challenging financial document questions. On the ViDoRe benchmark, the first evaluation specifically designed for visual document retrieval, our approach achieves 81.3% nDCG@5 compared to 67.0% for traditional parsing methods. But as our own evaluation shows, benchmarks only tell part of the story. The real difference is in understanding documents the way they were meant to be understood. Want to test your own system? The entire evaluation framework is ready to use. Just clone the repo, add your RAG implementation, and see how it performs on the same challenging financial document questions. The Speed Problem (And How We Solved It) Ok so we got to really good accuracy, but 'll be honest: our first implementation was slow. Visual understanding is computationally intensive, and ColPali's original multi-vector approach meant searching through millions of patch embeddings at scale. At 3-4 seconds per query for retrieval, it was impressive but not production-ready for our customers querying thousands of documents and demanding something fast. The breakthrough came from the MUVERA paper . Instead of searching through all patch embeddings independently, MUVERA reduces multi-vector search to single-vector similarity using fixed-dimensional encodings. Think of it as creating a "summary fingerprint" that preserves the rich patch interactions while being orders of magnitude faster to search. We paired this with Turbopuffer , a vector database built for exactly this use case. The results transformed our system, and our query latency went from 3-4s to 30ms. The math works out beautifully: we can now search millions of documents faster than traditional systems can parse a single PDF. What This Means for You Forget wrestling with document parsing libraries. Forget maintaining separate pipelines for text extraction, table detection, and OCR. Forget losing critical information every time a document doesn't fit your parsing assumptions. With visual document retrieval, you just send us your documents—PDFs, images, even photos of whiteboards—and search with natural language. It works particularly well for: Financial documents : Where charts and tables tell the real story Technical manuals : Where diagrams are worth thousands of words Invoices and receipts : Where layout and structure carry meaning Research papers : Where figures contain the actual findings Medical records : Where visual layouts indicate relationships The API is deliberately simple: upload your documents, search with queries like "show me all contracts with penalty clauses over $10K" or "find the deployment architecture diagram from last year's proposal." The Future: Beyond Simple Retrieval Visual document understanding solves the foundational problem, but real-world document workflows demand much more than single-shot retrieval. The future we're building toward involves documents that truly understand context, relationships, and complex reasoning chains. Multi-Document Intelligence : Today's systems treat each document as an island. Tomorrow's will understand how your Q3 financial report relates to the board deck from last month, how contract amendments reference the original agreement, and how technical specifications connect to implementation guides. At Morphik, we're already building multi-document retrieval that can trace information across entire document ecosystems, jumping seamlessly from page to page, document to document, following the logical threads that human experts would pursue. Agentic Document Reasoning : Simple Q&A is just the beginning. We're developing agentic systems that can perform multi-hop reasoning across documents—finding a contract clause, checking it against regulatory requirements in another document, then cross-referencing implementation details in a technical manual. Our knowledge graph capabilities help these agents understand not just what's in documents, but how different pieces of information relate to each other. Workflow Integration : The most powerful applications emerge when document understanding becomes part of broader business processes. Imagine systems that automatically flag contract discrepancies by comparing terms across multiple agreements, or that can trace a technical decision from initial requirements through design documents to implementation guides. We're building tools that don't just retrieve information—they understand it well enough to take action. The Gap We're Still Bridging : Despite these advances, we're honest about the limitations. Current systems, including ours, still fall short of true expert-level understanding. A human financial analyst doesn't just find numbers in a report—they understand market context, recognize subtle implications, and spot inconsistencies that require years of domain expertise. While our visual approach captures information that traditional parsing misses, we're still working toward systems that can provide the kind of ironclad guarantees that mission-critical decisions require. What's Next : The path forward involves deeper integration between visual understanding and domain knowledge. We're exploring how to combine our visual document retrieval with specialized knowledge graphs, how to build systems that can reason about causality and implication rather than just correlation, and how to provide the kind of confidence intervals and uncertainty quantification that enterprise applications demand. This isn't just about technology; it's about respecting how humans create and consume information. Documents are visual artifacts embedded in complex workflows, and they deserve to be understood not just as isolated objects, but as part of the rich, interconnected systems of knowledge that drive real decisions. Want to see how these capabilities can transform your document workflows? Try Morphik free at morphik.ai and join us in building a world where documents are understood, not dissected.
